what_this_is: The vendor's own two closed-form fit families for Magnetics powder cores, transcribed coefficient by coefficient: DC magnetization B(H) for 125 printed (material, core shape family, permeability) rows, and the permeability-versus-temperature polynomial for 54 printed (material, permeability) rows, plus the printed T/B/f stability columns as ranges. Every number is read off the PDF text layer and re-read off the rendered page for a sample; nothing here is digitised from a graph, interpolated between permeabilities, or filled in from memory.

source.pdf_pages_used: 130-134 (magnetization coefficients), 140-141 (temperature coefficients), 17 (printed stability table), 12 and 14 (High DC Bias variant coefficients)
source.printed_pages_used: 128-132 (magnetization coefficients), 138-139 (temperature coefficients), 15 (stability table), 10 and 12 (High DC Bias variants)
source.printed_page_offset: printed page = pdf page - 2 on every page used here; read off each page's own folio (pdf 131 prints 129, pdf 135 prints 133, pdf 141 prints 139, pdf 18 prints 16)
source.extraction: pymupdf text layer. Group names come from the merged first column of each printed table (find_tables), numbers from a word-level pass anchored on the printed header row, so a page whose column order differs cannot shift the coefficients. The printed stability table is rebuilt character by character from glyph origins, because the cell text as extracted comes back with the decimal point detached (.29% reads as 29%/. ). A page that yields a row of the wrong arity aborts the build rather than guessing a column.

magnetization.incremental_permeability: mu_r,differential = (dB/dH) / (mu0 * 79.5771) with H in Oe and B in T; it is computed by a numerical central difference on the printed fit, 2 * 1e-4 * H apart
magnetization.h_from_turns: H[Oe] = 0.4 * pi * N * I[A] / le[cm]  (CGS, the catalog's own relation)

temperature.printed: change compared with 25 C:  dmu/mu = a + b*T + c*T^2 + d*T^3 + e*T^4, T in degrees Celsius
temperature.evaluated_as: mu_change_fraction = a + b*T + c*T**2 + d*T**3 + e*T**4, times 100 for percent
temperature.sign_convention: the printed coefficient a is negative for every material, so the curve starts by falling below 25 C

units.permeability: dimensionless, the vendor's nominal mu for that row
units.a_b_c_d_e_x: coefficients exactly as printed (CGS scaling folded in)

magnetization_graphs.note: read off the axis labels in the text layer of the graph pages (pdf 125-129); the panels are log-spaced in H, some stop at 100 Oe and some at 300 Oe, and the page prints no numeric validity range for the fit, so this band is what the curves cover, not a promise from the vendor

temperature_graphs.note: the axis runs -60 to +200 C; the printed stability column on p.15 quotes the dynamic range over -50 to +100 C, and the running head of that column adds MATERIALS RATED TO 200 C

printing_anomalies.detail: all three rows print exactly a=-2.308E-03 b=8.497E-05 c=2.943E-07 d=0 e=0. Re-read off the rendered page at 200 dpi and identical there too, so this is how the catalog prints it.
both rows print a=-2.528E-03 b=9.211E-05 c=3.601E-07 d=0 e=0, again identical on the page
d=-2.000E-21 and e=1.000E-23. Over -60..200 C the d*T^3 term reaches 1e-14 and e*T^4 1.6e-14, i.e. they are padding digits rather than terms that shape the curve; kept as printed, not zeroed.

these five rows collapse to a nearly linear form (a 1.000E-03, d 1.000E-03 or 1.011E-03, x 0.833-1.021) while every other row in the table runs a 0.0123-0.1285 and x 1.25-2.20. B(H) stays positive and finite on the printed band, so the numbers are usable, but the row does not share the shape of its neighbours and must not be read as one - the tool reports a measured turnover where one exists.

c=1.118E-10, i.e. the quadratic numerator term is absent, and this is the only row whose fit peaks inside the plotted H band: dB/dH reaches zero at 23.8 Oe and the fit then falls (B(100 Oe) = 0.234 T). Its DC-bias twin of the same part integrates to 0.513 T at the same H, a 54 % difference - the largest disagreement in the table. Both numbers are printed by the vendor; this table reports both and picks neither.

magnetization_against_the_dc_bias_integr.method: data/dc_bias_fit.json carries the printed percent-of-mu_i fit of the same part; B[T] = 1e-4 * integral mu_r,differential dH over 0..H with mu_r,differential = permeability * percent/100. Two independent printed fits, one integrated and one evaluated.
magnetization_against_the_dc_bias_integr.reading: on the bulk of the table the two printed fits agree to well under a percent at 100 Oe, which is what makes them usable as a mutual check. The disagreement is not uniform: it lives at the two ends of the permeability scale (MPP 550u/300u above, Kool Mu Ultra and Edge low permeability below) where the vendor fits the curve in pieces. The integral, not the chord, is the right way to get B from a percent-mu fit: at 95 Oe on the 60u Kool Mu curve the chord gives 0.285 T and the integral 0.442 T, against a printed 0.441 T.

temperature_range_against_the_printed_st.method: the printed p.15 table lists, per material, the mu-vs-T dynamic range over -50..+100 C as a single number; the temperature fit predicts both ends of that band, so their difference can be compared with it.
temperature_range_against_the_printed_st.reading: nine materials, nine agreements inside 0.05 percentage points (worst 0.045 pp on Kool Mu, i.e. 2.945 % predicted against 2.9 % printed) from two independently printed quantities. This is the reason the temperature coefficients are carried at all.

printed_worked_example_page_25.printed: H = 95 Oe gives B = 0.441 T; H = 15.8 Oe gives B = 0.092 T (60u Kool Mu)
printed_worked_example_page_25.reading: 0.06 % from the printed 0.441 T at 95 Oe and 0.6 % at 15.8 Oe, so the magnetization family is the curve the catalog itself reads numbers off.

method_rejected.what: recovering mu_r from the slope of B(H) at H -> 0
method_rejected.detail: mu_r = x*a^(x-1)*(b - a*d) / (mu0*79.5771) does not reproduce the printed permeability: median error 36.9 % over the 61 toroid rows. The reason is that B(0) = a^x is not zero (5.3 mT for 60u Kool Mu), so this family is not a small-signal model and must not be used as one. Recorded here so that the rejection is not silently repeated.

cross_check.graphs_not_read_off_pixels: the curve panels are vector art with the axis labels in the text layer but the curves themselves are paths; no per-curve pixel or path read-out is carried here, so the cross-checks above are fit against fit, not fit against graph.

not_carried: no temperature dependence of Bsat: the catalog prints one saturation flux density per material (p.10) and no curve of it
no Steinmetz core-loss coefficients for powder cores, and no DC-bias correction of the loss curve
no per-part nominal weight: p.16 says See individual data sheets
the mu-vs-B and mu-vs-f columns are printed ranges, not curves

the two Perm/a/b/c tables that follow the High DC Bias magnetization blocks are a different fit form (a about 443, b 2.015, c 1.31 for High DC Bias XFlux) whose equation is not printed on the page; they are not carried rather than guessed

stability_printed_page_15.what_this_is: the printed PERMEABILITY vs. T, B, & f table: per material and permeability, the mu-vs-T dynamic range over -50..+100 C, the mu-vs-B dynamic range over 0..400 mT, and the frequency the permeability stays flat to. Ranges, not curves.
